solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shame about gardens with heart ripped out — an absolute mess

indicators.note: the regret is placed around the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: 'what a shame' and 'what a pity' say the same thing

indicators.note: with the inside of the word removed, only the outermost letters of gardens stay

explanation.surface: Someone laments a garden whose centre has been torn up, leaving a complete shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shame' is not disgrace here but the regretful 'what a shame'; 'gardens' supplies only its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A filthy, chaotic room is often called a sty or pigpen, the figurative sense of an animal enclosure.

clue.text: Shop quick to restrict damage

indicators.note: the quick word hems in the other one

parts.note: pacy means fast or quick
harm means damage

explanation.surface: A store moves fast to limit losses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy is a chemist's shop that dispenses medicines.

clue.text: Irregular fighter I left in care of harassed regular

indicators.note: placed in the keeping of the other piece, so put inside it
harassed letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A freedom fighter, with me gone, is left looking after a stressed soldier of the regular army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harassed' mixes REGULAR into GUERRLA; 'in care of' puts IL inside. 'Irregular' cleverly contrasts with 'regular'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is a member of an irregular, unofficial armed force, not part of a standing army.

clue.text: They bring sycophancy to a day in Ancient Rome

parts.note: dies is the Latin word for day

explanation.surface: Flatterers bring their fawning to a Roman day.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies are servile flatterers, people whose presence brings fawning obsequiousness.

clue.text: Money invested in major film about Panama firm

indicators.note: money put inside something, as in a financial investment, signals insertion
the film's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: an epic is a grand, large-scale film
a Panama is a kind of straw hat
M is the standard abbreviation for money in economics (M1, M2)

explanation.surface: Cash is put into a big movie about a company based in Panama.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: 'about' wraps the film round the hat, then 'invested in' slips the money in after the first letter. 'firm' looks like a company noun but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm denial is a forceful, emphatic one: both adjectives mean said with strong conviction.

clue.text: No Times clues (dodgy) around us — you'll get extreme care here

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the next piece
dodgy clues are unsound, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at the newspaper: dodgy clues are not from The Times, and our paper is where you find careful work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges NO TIMES CLUES, with US set among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Meticulousness is scrupulous attention to detail, the quality of taking very great care.

clue.text: Present encapsulating love given to popular, prominent girl

indicators.note: the word encloses the following pieces

parts.note: here means present, as in a roll call
O is a zero score, called love in tennis
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A gift wrapped with affection is given to a well-liked, well-known girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' only joins love and popular before both go inside; 'Present' is the adjective meaning in attendance, not a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A heroine is the leading female character of a story, the most prominent woman in it.

clue.text: Chosen player, brought in to beat colossus

indicators.note: the player is put inside the other word

parts.note: to tan is to beat, as in tanning someone's hide
in playground chase games the chosen chaser is 'it'

explanation.surface: A selected team member is drafted in to defeat a giant.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan is a person or thing of enormous size or power, like a colossus.

clue.text: Tooth — odds on one's captured in 'chewing requirement'

indicators.note: taken prisoner inside the other word

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews
SP, starting price, gives the odds in racing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tooth, and the odds on it being caught up in what is needed for chewing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link. SP is 'starting price', bookmakers' odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuspid is a canine tooth, the pointed one with a single cusp.

clue.text: Top personality vaguely sorry about spilled beer (mostly) and fruit

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
ego is one's sense of self or personality

indicators.note: the first muddled word goes round the second
vaguely arranged letters are muddled
spilled beer is in disarray, so its letters are scrambled
most but not all of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A senior figure is a bit apologetic about knocking over most of a pint and some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The muddled sorry is split round the spilled, shortened beer, so the solver must choose the split that yields a real word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cape gooseberry, or physalis, is a small orange berry in a papery husk, eaten as fruit.

clue.text: Region incorporating new sports ground

indicators.note: the region takes the other letter into its body

parts.note: a region is an area

explanation.surface: A district includes a newly built stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue where sporting contests are staged before spectators.

clue.text: Joint problem? It is provided by conjunction of skill and human resources

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
HR is the common abbreviation for human resources
taken as written, the two words run together

explanation.surface: A puzzle-like remark: some joint problem arises from combining talent with the personnel department.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Joint problem' could be a shared difficulty; here it is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is inflammation of the joints, causing pain and stiffness, so it is literally a problem in a joint.

clue.text: US state containing gold deposit

indicators.note: the state's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Maine is a state in the north-east of the USA
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An American state has a gold deposit within its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like a gold deposit in the surface; it is the definition of a glacial deposit.
explanation.definitionFit: A moraine is a mass of rock and debris left behind by a glacier, a geological deposit.

clue.text: Church opposing importing Italy's alcoholic drink

indicators.note: bringing something in from outside signals the insertion

parts.note: anti means against or opposing
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A church that opposes bringing in Italian booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' takes the Italy letter into the joined church and opposing pieces, at their junction.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Infection ought to lead to engineer, looking hot, being shunned

parts.note: a cold is a common viral infection
should means ought to

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: someone who is hot looks red in the face

explanation.surface: An infection should end up with a flushed engineer being avoided by colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead to engineer' gives just E, the word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cold-shouldered is to be deliberately ignored or snubbed, the same as being shunned.

clue.text: Get rid of a timeline that's incorrect

indicators.note: an incorrect timeline is wrongly ordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Throw out a chronology because it is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove it entirely, a plain synonym of discard.

clue.text: A call for assistance after swallowing foremost poisonous material

indicators.note: the signal takes in the other word, as if eating it

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
best means foremost or top

explanation.surface: Someone calls for help after swallowing something toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral once used in insulation whose fibres are toxic when inhaled.

clue.text: Leading philosopher's usual aims recur with working

indicators.note: the letters are put to work and so rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A top thinker's ordinary goals come back while he is busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading' is apt: Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor as well as a Stoic philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Aurelius, Roman emperor and author of the Meditations, was a Stoic philosopher who also led an empire.

clue.text: Singer bit put out when included in programme

indicators.note: the scrambled word is put inside the other

parts.note: a card is a printed programme, as at a race meeting

indicators.note: letters put out of place are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist is annoyed when only a minor part goes in the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges BIT into TBI, which goes into CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The catbird is a songbird whose call resembles a cat's mew; in crosswords any songbird is a singer.

clue.text: Prepare to fight, being terribly angered

indicators.note: terribly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a brawl, being furious.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's warning to get into a defensive stance before a bout begins.

clue.text: Overwhelms instances of trading involving millions

indicators.note: the trades enclose the other letter

parts.note: swaps are exchanges, acts of trading
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Deals worth millions swamp everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp is to flood or deluge, hence to overwhelm with too much.

clue.text: Laundry machine is no longer central feature around third of kitchens

parts.note: what is no longer the case was so, past tense

indicators.note: the hub wraps the following letter

parts.note: a hub is a central point or focus

indicators.note: take the third letter of kitchens

explanation.surface: A washing machine is no longer the focal point of a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of kitchens' is T, which 'around' places inside HUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A washtub is a tub for doing laundry, a basic manual washing device rather than an engine-driven one.

clue.text: Elevated songs about unknown country

indicators.note: the songs go around the next letter
in a down clue raised up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: airs are tunes or songs
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Uplifting songs about a mysterious land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' turns AIRS into SRIA, which goes round Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East bordering Turkey, Iraq and Lebanon.

clue.text: For example, engrossed by flashing leg in informal dress

indicators.note: something engrossed is absorbed, taken inside another piece
a flashing leg moves about, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone is absorbed by a glimpse of leg in a casual outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' scrambles LEG IN into NLIGE, and EG goes inside after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A negligee is a light, loose dressing gown or nightdress worn in private, hence a casual garment.

clue.text: Festival's to harm excavation — spots left incomplete

parts.note: to mar is to damage or harm
a dig is an archaeological excavation

indicators.note: the word is not finished, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A festival will damage an archaeological dig, leaving the site pockmarked and unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link; 'left incomplete' cuts the H from RASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is celebrated with carnivals and parades, notably in New Orleans.

clue.text: When tucking into tripe … you wouldn't be eating this!

indicators.note: the word goes inside the other, while the surface suggests eating

parts.note: tripe means nonsense, or rot
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: While you are tucking into a plate of tripe, you are plainly not eating a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripe' and 'tucking into' suggest food, but tripe is rot (nonsense).
explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat; a diner eating offal like tripe is not eating a roast joint at the same time.

clue.text: Cheap tickets, perhaps, through going in where the spectators are

indicators.note: the word enters the other piece

parts.note: the stands at a ground hold the spectators
by means through, as in 'by means of'

explanation.surface: Getting cheap seats by slipping into the crowd's area.
explanation.definitionFit: Standby tickets are sold cheaply at the last minute for seats left unsold; 'perhaps' marks them as an example.

clue.text: I named sea, wild sea, huge, but not hot

indicators.note: a wild sea is turbulent, so these letters are thrown into disorder
this excludes the letter that follows from the word before it

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A first-person boast: I gave my name to a sea, wild and enormous but cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not hot' drops H from HUGE, leaving UGE; 'wild' shuffles SEA plus UGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth King Aegeus of Athens drowned himself in the sea, which was then called the Aegean after him.
